p2: name stripped to 'Raṅgarāja', 'adhvarīndra' moved to titles
p5: name given as 'Kṛṣṇa' (śrī treated as honorific, consistent with Bālakṛṣṇa); śarman/jośī kept as titles; 'jośī' noted as upanāma (surname)
date: weekday normalized to Monday; VS/ŚS concordance checked (1755 VS = 1620 ŚS = 1698 CE)

persons.name: Kṛṣṇa
persons.evidence: jośī upanāmaka śrīkṛṣṇa śarma[[ṇe]] likhitvā dattaṃ ... pustakaṃ śrīkṛṣṇa jośī

purpose: written and given to Kṛṣṇa Jośī; merit dedicated to Kṛṣṇa (śrīkṛṣṇārpaṇam astu)
notes: The catalogue names Śrīkṛṣṇa Jośī as scribe, but according to the colophon Sundara, son of Bālakṛṣṇa Daivajña, wrote the copy and gave it to Kṛṣṇa Jośī ('jośī upanāmaka' = surname Jośī), who is the owner ('pustakaṃ śrīkṛṣṇa jośī'). The name may be Śrīkṛṣṇa, as the catalogue gives it. Here 'śrī' is taken as an honorific. The two eras agree: VS 1755 = ŚS 1620 = 1698 CE. 'śarma[[ṇe]]' is an editorial restoration of the dative. 'apya' is a corrupt form of Appayya. 'varada' in 'raṃgarājādhvarīṃdravaradasūnor' is read as an epithet and is not treated as a separate person.
